label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 8, samples with blocking 27

A.rule: a non-ledger_app session blocked ledger_app sessions in 27 samples

report.summary: Transfer 500s and slow requests coincide with ledger_app sessions blocked by an idle-in-transaction session (4672) from 19:13:27 to 19:14:19. The link to the 500s is inferred from timing only. The outbox consumer is healthy.

findings.claim: Blocked ledger_app sessions waited up to 2.01s on session 4672, which was idle in transaction, between 19:13:27 and 19:14:19.
findings.reason: Historical blocker samples show repeated waits on one idle-in-transaction session, with 27 of 105 samples showing blocking.

findings.claim: The transfers route had 99 HTTP 500s (15%) and p95 of 2.26s and p99 of 4.18s, consistent with lock waits.
findings.reason: The slow and failing requests match the blocking window in magnitude, but no per-request timing or error text ties them to those waits.

findings.claim: The connection pool was not exhausted, so the slowness came from DB lock waits rather than pool starvation.
findings.reason: There were 0 acquisition timeouts, 0 pending borrowers and a 5 ms maximum acquire time. Active connections reached only 7 of 10, in the 19:13:28-19:14:18 scrapes.

findings.claim: The outbox consumer was healthy: all 562 deliveries succeeded in about 71ms. A pre-existing backlog of 296 FAILED rows is stuck and unchanged, so it does not explain the symptom.
findings.reason: Delivery logs show only successes and timings are stable. The failed count stayed flat at 296 and the oldest undelivered age was already about 5300s at window start.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2s, and the 500s were not matched to individual blocked requests or error messages.
The origin of session 4672 and the cause of the old 296 FAILED outbox rows are not identified.
next_checks: Identify session 4672's application, its last query and when its transaction started, and compare that with the 500 timestamps.
Check the application error logs for the 500 responses to see whether they are lock-timeout or statement-timeout errors.

alternatives.reason: Deliveries all succeeded in about 71ms with no errors.
alternatives.hypothesis: Outbox delivery or consumer slowness caused the failures

alternatives.reason: There were no acquisition timeouts or pending borrowers.
alternatives.hypothesis: Connection pool exhaustion caused the failures and slowness
